## 2. What was done this session

### R7 — correct affirmatively-false comments (`21078e2b4`)

Scoped tightly to statements that were *false about current behaviour*, not cosmetic
staleness. The ~15 stale `SessionLock` mentions were explicitly left out of scope.

- **`collection-service.ts`** — `recordClaimSeen` "self-acquires the session lock" was
  false; it opens its own SQLite session transaction (`mutateSession`), which cannot nest.
- **`lifecycle-command-service.ts`** — rewrote the explicit-path (`#driveSubstepExplicit`)
  lock-ordering / ABBA proof. Verified current reality:
  - `SessionLock` and the run-state file lock are replaced by SQLite transactions.
  - `runGuardedParentAdvance`'s open-delegated-children check is an **in-transaction SQLite
    guard** (`ParentAdvanceGuard`), not a lock.
  - `releaseRunbook` commits a **SQLite session transaction** (`mutateSession`), not `SessionLock`.
  - The only live cross-lock file-lock edge is **`DelegationLock → CompletionLock`**
    (`recordChildCompletion` holds parent `DelegationLock`, calls `recordManualCompletion`
    which acquires `CompletionLock`).
  - `RunStateLock` is defined but **never actually acquired in production** — run state is SQLite.
  - Also fixed the two satellite comments in the same method citing the dead `SessionLock` edge.
- **`state.ts`** — three sites: class doc + `save()` now say SQLite (`.rundown/rundown.db`),
  not `.rundown/runs/` JSON; `loadSession`'s `@throws` no longer claims the #519
  legacy-format / unparseable-JSON throws that typed-column reconstruction made impossible.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — dropped the dead `RunbookStateManager.withRunStateLock` reference (that
  method exists nowhere in the tree) and named the real live narrow-DI consumer:
  `DelegationLockLike` injected into the lifecycle seam, wrapping `heldLock` inline.

Verification: `pnpm run lint` + `pnpm run check:types` green. No behavioural change.

### R6 — Finish state-only session-mutation ownership refusals (plan lines 767–884)

**Large, invasive. Sits directly on the SQLite recovery-refusal surface — the coordination
hazard (see §4).**

- Type every ownership-sensitive session mutation as one outer
  `SessionMutationResult<T>` union: `committed | execution-in-progress | recovery-required`.
  Domain unions (`ClaimRunbookResult`, `ReleaseRunbookResult`, `UnstashForClaimIdResult`)
  stay as values of the `committed` arm — do **not** flatten them in.
- **11 methods widened in one commit:** `issueRunControlClaim`,
  `pushRunbookWithRunControlClaim`, `claimRunbook`, `releaseRunbook`, `releaseRunbooks`,
  `pruneClaimsForChildren`, `popRunbook`, `stash`, `stashRunbook`, `unstashForClaimId`,
  `unstash`.
- **Exempt (do not widen):** `recordClaimSeen` (total/best-effort, excluded from guard
  triggers), `resetForPruneAll` (explicit invalid-state recovery op), `pushRunbook`
  (stack-only, `Promise<void>`).
- Add `RunbookStoreTxn.pendingRecovery(runId)` ambient read on `txn.tx` (do NOT call
  `RunbookStore.readPendingRecovery` inside a txn — it opens a separate driver read).
  Preflight each affected run; a hit returns `recovery-required`, else mutate. The trigger
  catch can only ever produce `execution-in-progress`.
- Normalize trigger aborts at the repository boundary: both drivers give
  `error.message === 'execution_in_progress'`, only node:sqlite adds `ERR_SQLITE_ERROR`.
  Classify by exact message; re-throw everything else. Never parse a message to infer
  `recovery-required`.
- Multi-run mutation: preflight run ids **in caller-supplied order**, return the first
  refusal, transaction stays all-or-none.
- Add the **CAS-zero-row property** (arbitrary stale `state_version`/`claim_generation` →
  zero-row update aborts and rolls back the whole txn). The parent-linkage property is R8's,
  not R6's.
- **~10 CLI/core callers** must switch exhaustively — a refusal must never be consumed as
  `null`, ignored after `await`, or re-synthesized. Fresh inventory below (§5).
- Verify: focused core `__tests__/runbook/` + CLI pop/prune/stash/claim-and-launch suites,
  both `check:types`. Commit: `fix(core): type session ownership refusals`.

### R8 — Atomic initial claim/link, remove vacuous linkage versioning (plan lines 927–1058)

**Depends on R2 + R3 + R6.**

- Verified premise: the product has **no A→B relink operation**, so `parent_linkage_version`
  can never legitimately advance. Remove the column, `LinkageVersion`, `assertLinkageVersion`,
  `CommitRow.parentLinkageVersion`, and the comparison in `classifyCommitRow`.
- Move the split CLI claim-then-link sequence into core: add
  `SessionService.claimAndInitialLink` and `rollbackInitialLink` (one immediate transaction:
  validate parent/child/token/frame/entry + R2 liveness, refuse already-linked as replay,
  insert claim, rewrite only the matching parent delegation's `childRunId` under observed
  `state_version`, call R2's `afterAuthoritativeStateWrite` once, commit all-or-none).
- **Delete `updateStepDelegationChildRunId`** from the CLI pipeline; the CLI must not
  reconstruct/patch `SubstepState`. Route only orphan adoption + fresh-child creation through
  the new method; the already-linked replay branch keeps calling ordinary `claimRunbook`.
- Bump SQLite `SCHEMA_VERSION` **2 → 3** (Rundown `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `1`).
  Update `driver-contract.test.ts` version assertion. Same hard-reject/no-migration `RD-305`
  behaviour as R3 — announce in the commit body that every `.rundown/rundown.db` becomes
  unopenable.
- Structural properties (all-or-none, idempotent re-link, no-replace-live-link, token-reissue
  tombstone-once, `lastSeenAt` no-bump, terminalization one-status-UPDATE) over both adapters.
- Commit: `fix(core): make delegated claim and initial link atomic`.

## 4. Coordination hazard (READ BEFORE R6/R8)

A second session has been actively committing to this same branch in the **SQLite recovery
area** — recent commits `2b86d2188` (share delegation-linkage schema), `ebc396411` (harden
sqlite recovery), `9edfa08ef` (harden storage driver lifecycle), `c1298a91d` (hydrate
recovery runs), `6f1e323fe` (dead-owner recovery protocol).

**R6 sits directly on the recovery-refusal surface** (`runbook-store.ts`,
`session-service.ts`, the trigger-abort classification, `pendingRecovery`). R8 shares the
same files. Per the plan, tasks sharing `runbook-store.ts` / `session-service.ts` / driver
contract tests / claim surfaces **must not run in parallel in one worktree.**

**Signal as of this writing:** the other session's last recovery-surface commit was ~16 hours
ago; the only newer touch to `runbook-store.ts` is this session's 1-line lint modifier drop.
That is *suggestive* of the other session being idle, **not proof.** Before starting R6:
confirm the other session is clear of the recovery area, and re-run the R6 caller inventory
(§5) so any newly-landed caller lands in the same commit.

R7 (done) and the lint fix touched none of the recovery logic.

## 6. Conventions (from CLAUDE.md) that bit or matter here

- State machine in `@rundown-org/core` owns all logic; CLI/mcp/plugin are thin wrappers.
- **Never migrate persisted state**; reject incompatible state, no compatibility shims.
- **SCHEMA_VERSION stays at 1** for Rundown persisted state (`state.ts`); the *SQLite*
  `storage/schema.ts::SCHEMA_VERSION` is the one that moves (→3 at R8). Do not conflate.
- **Biome** is the formatter/linter of record for `.ts/.js/.mjs` (single quotes); Prettier
  only owns `*.md`. Do NOT run prettier on `.ts`. Biome does **not** honour `eslint-disable`
  — use `// biome-ignore <rule>: <reason>`. (This was the `mutate-scoped.mjs` failure.)
- Pre-commit hook runs lint-staged (biome format + lint on staged files; prettier on `*.md`).
- Use `isError`/`isNodeError`/`getErrorMessage`, never `Error.isError` directly.
- `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is on: never pass `{ guard: undefined }`; omit the key.
- Commit only when a task is green; run `pnpm run verify` before any push.
- Scoped mutation: `node scripts/mutate-scoped.mjs core <src> <testFiles>` (one comma-list
  per flag; repeated `--mutate`/`--testFiles` collapse to last-wins). Core is excluded from
  the per-PR mutation matrix, so a hand-run scoped campaign is core's only mutation signal.
